reviewer.method: Round-4 (v9) independent pass. This round's sole purpose was fixing stale observation timestamps on shot-1 through shot-4, which findings-preview-v8.json (and v7/v6 before it) had carried forward verbatim without re-checking them against the current shot boundaries. Confirmed the root cause myself: read output/preview-reference/evidence.json's plan.shots array directly -- scene 1's total span is unchanged at exactly 0-15.0s (SCENE_MIN floor), but the internal cut points shifted because Vidka's opening line in shot-0 was reworded and is now longer (~5.6s of narration vs ~3s before): shot-0 is now 0-2.838s (was ~0-2.3s), shot-1 is now 2.838-5.677s (was ~2.3-4.4s), shot-2 is now 5.677-9.461s (was ~4.4-7.3s), shot-3 is now 9.461-11.123s (was ~7.3-9.6s), and shot-4 is now 11.123-15.0s (was ~9.6-15.0s). Every v8 observation time for shot-1/2/3/4 predates this shift and falls outside the shot's current window (e.g. v8's shot-1 time=2.3 is now before shot-1 even starts at 2.838), which is exactly why the upstream b-style-reference-review.mjs validator rejects them. shot-0 and shot-5 were left untouched because every one of their v8 observation times already falls inside their respective current windows (shot-0: 0-2.838s, all v8 times 0.0-2.83 in range; shot-5: 15.0-17.821s, all v8 times 15.0-17.8 in range) -- re-checked this by direct comparison before excluding them from rework, not assumed. For shots 1-4 I did not rubber-stamp the old prose: I independently re-extracted frames from the current output/preview.mp4 with ffmpeg at each shot's new start, one or more mid-points, and end, and visually inspected every one before writing a new observation. Shot-1 (2.838-5.677s): frames at 2.90/3.10/3.30/3.70/3.95/4.05/4.15/4.35/5.00/5.50/5.60s confirm Vidka's close-up hand-to-forehead distress pose at the start, a switch to a speaking pose (hand down, mouth open) somewhere between 3.30s (still distress) and 3.70s (already speaking) timed to the caption's second clause 'tetapi malah bingung memilih.', and a return to the distress pose somewhere between 4.15s (still speaking) and 4.35s (already distress), holding through to the 5.677s cut -- content matches the old baseline's description exactly, only the absolute times move. Shot-2 (5.677-9.461s): frames at 5.80/6.30/6.80/7.30/8.00/9.30s confirm the desk scene with Herry and Vidka, two separate opaque sheets, Herry's red pointer stroke drawing in progressively from about 6.3s to full length by 6.8s, Vidka turning with a smile by 8.0s, and the red frame around 'catatanmu' drawing in and completing by 9.3s, just before the cut -- matches the old baseline's choreography. Shot-3 (9.461-11.123s): frames at 9.50/9.80/10.20/10.60/11.00s confirm Vidka's sweeping arm motion with the two article sheets briefly rendered as overlapping transparent outlines mid-slide (the same minor, previously-noted drawing lapse, unchanged in severity) before settling as two separate sheets further left by the shot's end -- matches the old baseline. Shot-4 (11.123-15.0s): frames at 11.20/12.00/12.50/13.00/13.50/14.80s confirm the spiral notebook with the red 'catatan awal Vidka' label, the pencil writing 'Bagaimana kelompok kami' then 'menjaga tempo?' line by line (first line complete by 12.0s, second line complete by 12.5s), an underline drawing in between about 13.0s and 13.5s, and Vidka's raised-finger 'got it' smiling reaction visible by 14.8s -- matches the old baseline's description exactly. No regression or genuine new problem was found in any of the four shots at their corrected times; every check keeps its prior pass/unmet status because the fresh look substantively confirms the same content the old (mistimed) observations described -- only the time values and, where the old text depended on the stale schedule (e.g. shot-1's typography_captions, which had wrongly cited shot-2's Herry caption as appearing inside shot-1), the wording were corrected. shot-0, shot-5, shot-6 through shot-13, the baseline section, the blocking_issues array (empty, unchanged) and the limits section are carried forward byte-for-byte from review/findings-preview-v8.json: I did not re-view their frames or alter a single character, since their content is unaffected by this round's fix and their existing times are already valid against the current plan.shots windows. full_playback is also carried forward unchanged, since its sampled times (0.0, 0.4, 15.0, 33.6, 45.0, 54.6, 57.3, 59.5) all fall inside scene boundaries unaffected by the internal scene-1 shift (0.0 and 0.4 are within shot-0, which was confirmed in-range above).
